sources.title: Complete Suppression of the m=2/n=1 NTM Using ECCD on DIII-D
sources.version: GA-A24317, May 2003; conference preprint; not the 2004 Nuclear Fusion publication

read_scope.figures: 1–4, directly inspected all four in rendered body pages
read_scope.references: all listed references read as bibliographic entries, not their cited full texts

sources.experiment: DIII-D tokamak, finite-amplitude m/n=2/1 NTM ECCD control
diagnostics: ECE and MSE geometry in Fig. 1
driven current from CQL3D, not direct measurement

figure_evidence.1: geometry, ECE/MSE, q surfaces and EC trajectories
figure_evidence.2: complete vs partial suppression time histories with NBI/beta feedback
figure_evidence.3: position sweep, amplitude minimum as q=2 and deposition locations coincide
figure_evidence.4: modified Rutherford equilibrium width comparison; 10% gyrotron power uncertainty

limitations: finite-amplitude NTM control, not FKR linear growth measurement
40 kA current and deposition profiles modeled
width matched using island width, not independent blind prediction
not_read: references used for omitted coefficients of the modified Rutherford model

sources.title: Laboratory Observation of Resistive Electron Tearing in a Two-Fluid Reconnecting Current Sheet
sources.version: 5-page author manuscript in existing repository papers/E448.pdf; journal DOI version identified

read_scope.body: all text, methods, results, discussion and references
read_scope.figures: 1–5 directly inspected; Fig. 1 apparatus, Figs. 2–5 results

sources.experiment: MRX driven antiparallel reconnection, collisional argon
diagnostics: Poincare-Hopf winding check of O/X identification
reconnection electric field and current, Spitzer-resistivity comparison

figure_evidence.2: island chains, reconstructed flux and field reversal
figure_evidence.3: island number and sheet aspect versus S; SD vs SEM distinguished
figure_evidence.4: time traces including approximately 10% conservative rate uncertainty
figure_evidence.5: rate change event statistics; most positive, mean about 10% normalized rate enhancement per formation event

limitations: not fully quantitative 2D eigenmode comparison for measured density/Hall/compressibility and finite aspect
small-island flux contours depend on interpolation; independent winding method used
not_read: independently retrieved journal final PDF beyond existing author manuscript

sources.title: Experimental Evidence of Plasmoids in High-beta Magnetic Reconnection
sources.version: 7-page PRL PDF publicly hosted by author institution, includes appendix

read_scope.body: full body, methods appendix, conclusion and reference list

sources.experiment: OMEGA EP laser-driven magnetized CH plasma bubbles, high-beta current sheet
diagnostics: TNSA proton radiography, different energies select times in one shot
Monge-Ampere inversion gives path-integrated magnetic field
plasma parameters include separate nominally equivalent OMEGA Thomson-scattering measurements

figure_evidence.3: inferred path-integrated B, flux and islands
figure_evidence.4: normal-field sign changes, O/X topology evidence
figure_evidence.6: island widths vs time; central/right no resolved growth; fast left expansion geometry-confounded

limitations: path-integrated inverse problem with incident fluence, trajectory mapping and energy spread assumptions
local B depends on path length
fast changing background not steady Sweet-Parker/FKR eigenproblem
lack of simultaneous side-on reconstruction leaves 3D uncertainty
typical expected growth in available window below spatial resolution
CH treated as effective ion species in quoted scale estimates
not_read: raw radiographic films and source data
prior method papers beyond discussion in present appendix
